questions.q: What is a 'segment' in AWS X-Ray?
options: A fixed percentage of requests selected for tracing
One service's record of the work it did for a request, within a trace
A CloudWatch alarm threshold
A section of the X-Ray console UI
questions.explain: A segment is the record one service contributes to a trace — its start time, end time, and metadata for the work it did handling that request.

questions.q: How does the X-Ray service map get built?
options: An engineer manually draws the architecture diagram
Automatically, from the trace data X-Ray has already collected
It is imported from CloudFormation templates
It requires a separate paid add-on
questions.explain: The service map is generated automatically from real trace data — no separate architecture description is needed, similar to Azure's Application Map.

questions.q: A checkout request took 4 seconds total, and its trace timeline shows the 'call payment gateway' subsegment took 3.8 seconds of that. What does this tell you?
options: The payment gateway call is the dominant source of the request's latency
The database is the bottleneck
The trace is corrupted and should be discarded
Sampling missed this request
questions.explain: Reading a trace timeline means finding which segment or subsegment's bar dominates the total duration — here, the payment gateway call clearly accounts for nearly all the latency.

questions.q: Why does X-Ray use sampling instead of tracing every single request?
options: Tracing every request is technically impossible
Tracing everything would be costly to store and process, and mostly redundant since similar fast requests look alike
Sampling is required by AWS billing policy
X-Ray can only trace requests that fail
questions.explain: Sampling rules trace a representative subset of requests (by default, the first request per second plus 5% of the rest) to balance visibility against cost and volume.

questions.q: What can a sampling rule be configured to always capture, regardless of the general sampling rate?
options: Only requests from a specific IP address
Requests that return an error
Requests made on weekends only
Nothing — sampling rates are fixed and cannot be customized
questions.explain: Sampling rules are configurable — for example, you can always trace error responses even while sampling down the volume of successful, fast requests.
